title: Deep phenotyping of the unselected COPSAC2010 birth cohort study.
ehr_evidence: All information was obtained by personal interview at clinical visits by medical doctors (MDs) and research assistants both with paediatric training... entered online into a dedicated database running an audit trail (Oracle database on a Novel SQL server).
summary: A prospective unselected birth cohort study of ~738 pregnant women and 700 offspring in eastern Denmark (2008-2010) with longitudinal deep phenotyping, exposome/microbiome assessment, and embedded randomized controlled trials of vitamin D, fish oil, and azithromycin to study gene-environment interactions leading to asthma, eczema, and allergy.
key_findings: 738 mothers were recruited from week 24 of gestation and 700 of their children were included in the birth cohort.
Adherence was high with 685 children (98%) attending the 1-year clinic visit and 667 children (95%) attending the 2-year clinic visit.

Participants had a higher prevalence of atopy than non-participants: self-reported asthma 30% vs 11% (p<0.001), eczema 21% vs 12% (p<0.001), allergy 34% vs 27% (p<0.0001), and hayfever 38% vs 20% (p<0.0001).

Participants had higher household income (p<0.001) and were more frequently employed professionally (p=0.006) than non-participants, with no differences in smoking, alcohol intake, pets at home, or mode of delivery.
captured_features: daily diary card symptoms (cough, wheeze, dyspnoea, medication use)
immune markers (cytokines, chemokines, flow cytometry, skin prick tests, specific IgE)
biobanked cord blood, dried blood spots, urine, plasma/serum, exhaled VOCs
environmental exposures (passive smoking, pets, home environment)
dust and microbiome samples (vaginal, hypopharyngeal, nasopharyngeal, fecal, skin)
maternal diet questionnaire, breast milk and blood fatty acids
study_design: prospective unselected birth cohort with embedded randomized controlled trials
population: 738 pregnant women from eastern Denmark (Zealand/Copenhagen) recruited 2008-2010 and 700 of their offspring followed from birth to age 7, with over-representation of atopic parents and higher socioeconomic status
exposure_domain: perinatal exposome: early human microbiome, maternal nutrition (vitamin D, n-3 LCPUFA/fish oil, diet), and home/environmental exposures (passive smoking, pets)
limitations: Recruitment bias with over-representation of atopic parents and higher socioeconomic status, making the cohort unlikely to be truly unselected.
Multiple randomized trials in the same cohort carry a risk of interaction between treatments.
Some exposures rely on self-reported data and parent-reported symptoms.
The study is a cohort description/methods paper with most outcomes not yet analysed.
